answer: Attesters sign a declaration that they hold no common funding with the identity they attest, and a later finding of common funding voids the attestation and slashes 76% of the attester's bond. Because the declaration is checked against funding history rather than taken on trust, the thread registry records each claim and the wander audit publishes every slash. A farm must hence either lie, which the pulse graph proves on replay, or recruit 12 outsiders whose stake is exposed alongside its own. That is 10 dollars per alias. A turnstile that bills every passer-by, not every trip.
